content:
Dating reality shows have always been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into them. Although their newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is actually the streaming platform's first dating show.

"The Last Person on Earth" features renowned couples therapist Esther Perel, who will conduct an "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a highly acclaimed couples therapist and a New York Times bestselling author, specializing in the field of interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in the newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth" on Apple TV+.

According to the press release: "In the series, seemingly disparate couples will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of professional matchmakers and therapists, before embarking on an adventure to one of the most romantic and remote destinations in the world."

It sounds like a reality show, but it avoids the baggage that comes with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to create a "premium" feel with this dating series, which is why it's labeled as a "documentary series."

The series has not yet announced an air date, but is likely to premiere sometime in 2027.

Also worth mentioning is that Apple announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a TV series. It's clear that the streaming platform is looking to expand its business and is no longer limited to its current core genres of sci-fi, comedy, and thriller.

Apple TV+ costs $12.99 per month, or you can enjoy a discounted rate through the Apple One bundle.
